Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 49, verse 1:

The explanation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] before Allah and His Messenger, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾ (1)

By His words, exalted is His remembrance, ﴿O you who have believed﴾, He means: O you who have affirmed the oneness of Allah and the prophethood of His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿Do not put [yourselves] before Allah and His Messenger﴾ means: do not hasten to decide a matter in your wars or your religion before Allah and His Messenger have decided it for you, lest you rule contrary to the command of Allah and the command of His Messenger. It is related from the Arabs: "So-and-so goes before his imam (yuqaddimu bayna yadayi imamihi)," meaning he hastens to command and forbid without him.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what is similar to what we have said, although their wording differs in clarifying its meaning.

Mention of those who said this:

• Ali related to us, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿do not put [yourselves] before Allah and His Messenger﴾: he said, do not say anything contrary to the Book and the Sunnah.

• Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] before Allah and His Messenger﴾ ... the verse, he said: they were forbidden to speak before His speech.

• Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa related to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] before Allah and His Messenger﴾, he said: do not presume to decide anything over the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until Allah decides it upon his tongue.

• Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] before Allah and His Messenger﴾: it was mentioned to us that some people used to say, "If only it had been revealed concerning such-and-such, it would have stipulated such-and-such." He said: Allah, mighty and majestic, disliked that, and pre-empted it in this matter.

And al-Hasan said: some Muslims slaughtered before the prayer of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of sacrifice, so the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) ordered them to repeat the slaughter.

• Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] before Allah and His Messenger﴾, he said: some people used to say, "If only it had been revealed concerning such-and-such, if only it had been revealed concerning such-and-such." And al-Hasan said: they were a people who sacrificed before the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed, so the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered them to repeat the slaughter.

• I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd related to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words ﴿O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] before Allah and His Messenger﴾, that it means in fighting, and whatever of their affairs it is not right to decide except by His command, of the laws of their religion. [[As it stands in the original; the likely correct reading is: "and everything of their affairs..." etc.]]

• Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb related to us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the words of His majestic praise ﴿O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] before Allah and His Messenger﴾: do not cut off a matter without Allah and His Messenger.

• Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan (﴿O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] before Allah and His Messenger﴾): he said, do not decide a matter without the Messenger of Allah.

As for the vocalization of the verb ﴿lā tuqaddimū﴾ with a damma on the tā' (tuqaddimū), it is the reading of the reciters of the major cities (qurra' al-amsar), and it is the reading I do not consider permissible to recite contrary to, because the consensus of the authoritative reciters rests upon it. It is related from the Arabs: "qaddimtu fi kadha" and "taqaddamtu fi kadha," and according to this usage it would have been permissible to read ﴿lā taqaddamū﴾ with a fatha on the tā' [[with the dāl shaddah; this is a well-known reading of Ya'qub al-Hadrami]].

And His words ﴿and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾

He means: and fear Allah, O you who have believed, in your speech, lest you say what Allah and His Messenger have not permitted you to say, and in your other affairs; and be mindful of Him. Indeed, Allah is Hearing of what you say, Knowing of what you intend by your speech when you speak. Nothing of the inner thoughts of your breasts, or of your other affairs and the affairs of others, is hidden from Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 49, verse 2:

On the interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, and do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another, lest your deeds become worthless while you do not perceive﴾ (49:2).

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Messenger of God, confronting him with speech and being harsh in your address to him. ﴿And do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another﴾ means: do not call out to him as some of you call out to others, saying: "O Muhammad, O Muhammad, O Prophet of God, O Prophet of God, O Messenger of God."

The exegetes have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿And do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another﴾, he said: Do not call out to him with a call, but with gentle speech: "O Messenger of God."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another﴾: they used to speak loudly to him and raise their voices, so God admonished them and forbade them from that.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: they used to raise their voices and speak loudly in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, so they were admonished and forbidden from that.

I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet﴾ ... the verse: it is like His saying: ﴿Do not make the calling of the Messenger among you like your calling of one another﴾. God forbade them to call out to him as some of them call out to others, and commanded them to honor and glorify him, and to address him, when they call him, by the title of prophethood.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Hubab told us, saying: Abu Thabit ibn Thabit Qays ibn al-Shammas told us, saying: my paternal uncle Isma'il ibn Muhammad ibn Thabit ibn Shammas told me, from his father, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, and do not speak loudly to him﴾, Thabit sat on the road weeping. 'Asim ibn 'Adi of Banu al-'Ajlan passed by him and said: "What makes you weep, O Thabit?" He said: "Because of this verse; I fear it was revealed concerning me, and I am a man with a loud, high voice." 'Asim went off to the Messenger of God ﷺ, and was overcome with weeping. He came to his wife Jamila, daughter of 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, and said to her: "When I enter the stable of my horse, tighten the bolt on the door with a nail." She struck it with a nail until it came out bent, and he said: "I will not leave until God takes my soul, or the Messenger of God ﷺ is pleased with me." 'Asim came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and informed him of his situation. He said: "Go and call him to me." 'Asim came to the place but did not find him, so he went to his family and found him in the stable of the horse. He said to him: "The Messenger of God ﷺ is calling you." He said: "Break the bolt." They both went out and came to the Prophet of God ﷺ. The Messenger of God ﷺ said to him: "What makes you weep, O Thabit?" He said: "I am loud-voiced, and I fear that this verse was revealed concerning me: ﴿Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, and do not speak loudly to him﴾." The Messenger of God ﷺ said to him: "Are you not pleased to live praiseworthy, to be killed a martyr, and to enter Paradise?" He said: "I am pleased with the glad tidings of God and His Messenger; I will never raise my voice again above the Messenger of God." Then God revealed ﴿Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of God are those whose hearts God has tested for piety﴾ ... the verse.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub told us, from Hafs, from Shamir ibn 'Atiyyah, who said: Thabit ibn Qays ibn al-Shammas came to the Messenger of God ﷺ while he was grieved, and he said: "O Thabit, what is this I see in you?" He said: "A verse I recited last night; I fear that my deeds have become worthless: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet﴾." He had deafness in his ear. He said: "O Prophet of God, I fear that I have raised my voice and spoken loudly to you, and that my deeds have become worthless while I do not perceive it." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Walk upon the earth vigorously, for you are one of the people of Paradise."

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah told us, saying: Ayyub told us, from 'Ikrimah, who said: When ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet﴾ ... the verse was revealed, Thabit ibn Qays said: "I used to raise my voice above the voice of the Prophet ﷺ and speak loudly to him, so I am among the people of the Fire." He sat in his house, and the Messenger of God ﷺ missed him and asked about him. A man said: "He is my neighbor, and if you wish I will find out his condition for you." He said: "Yes." So he went to him and said: "The Messenger of God ﷺ has missed you and asked about you." He said: "This verse was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet﴾ ... the verse, and I used to raise my voice above the voice of the Messenger of God ﷺ and speak loudly to him, so I am among the people of the Fire." The man returned to the Messenger of God and informed him, and he said: "Rather, he is among the people of Paradise." Then, on the day of Yamama, the people fled, and he said: "Fie upon these people and what they worship, and fie upon these people and what they do. O assembly of the Ansar, clear a path for me, that perhaps I may fight by its heat for an hour." And there was a man standing in a breach, and he killed and was killed.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, that Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas said: When ﴿Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet﴾ was revealed, he said: "O Prophet of God, I feared that I had been destroyed. God forbade us to raise our voices above your voice, and I am a man of loud voice; and God forbade a man to love to be praised for what he did not do, and I find myself loving to be praised; and God forbade pride, and I find myself loving beauty." The Messenger of God ﷺ said to him: "O Thabit, are you not pleased to live praiseworthy, to be killed a martyr, and to enter Paradise?" So he lived praiseworthy, and was killed a martyr on the day of Musaylima.

'Ali ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: Mu'ammal told us, saying: Nafi' ibn 'Umar ibn Jumayl al-Jumahi told us, saying: Ibn Abi Mulayka narrated to me, from al-Zubayr, who said: "A delegation, I think he said of Tamim, came to the Prophet ﷺ, among them al-Aqra' ibn Habis. Abu Bakr spoke to the Prophet ﷺ asking that he appoint him over his people. 'Umar said: 'Do not do it, O Messenger of God.' They argued until their voices were raised in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ. Abu Bakr said to 'Umar: 'You only intended to oppose me.' 'Umar said: 'I did not intend to oppose you.'" He said: "And the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet﴾ ... to His saying ﴿and a great reward﴾." He said: "'Umar never spoke to the Prophet ﷺ after that without the Prophet ﷺ having to hear him repeat it." He said: "Ibn al-Zubayr did not mention his grandfather, meaning Abu Bakr."

* *

As for His saying ﴿lest your deeds become worthless﴾:

It means: lest your deeds be made worthless, going to waste, with no reward for you in them, and no recompense for raising your voices above the voice of your Prophet and speaking loudly to him as some of you speak loudly to others.

The grammarians have differed concerning the meaning of this. Some of the Kufan grammarians said: its meaning is "your deeds would become worthless." He said: in it there is jazm and raf' when "lest" (an) is replaced by "la". He said: it is in the reading of 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud) ﴿fa-tahbata a'malukum﴾, which is evidence for the permissibility of jazm. Some of the Basran grammarians said: "an tahbata a'malukum" means: for fear that your deeds become worthless, as it is said: "Support the wall lest it lean (an yamil)."

* *

As for His saying ﴿while you do not perceive﴾:

It means: while you do not know and are not aware.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 49, verse 3:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah - those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for piety. For them is forgiveness and a great reward.﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Indeed, those who restrain (yakuffuna) the raising of their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah. The root of al-ghadd (lowering) is restraint with gentleness. From it comes ghadd al-basar (lowering the gaze), which is restraining it from looking, as Jarir said:

"So lower your gaze, for you are of Numayr... You have not reached Ka'b nor Kilab."

[The verse is by Jarir ibn al-Khatafi, from a qasida in which he satirizes al-Ra'i al-Numayri the poet. (His Diwan, 64.) He says to him: lower your gaze, meaning restrain your sight in humiliation and abasement. This is the point of evidence in His words, "who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah," and it is from this usage. In Lisan al-Arab, under gh-d-d, it says: "He lowered his glance and his gaze, lowering it (yaghudduhu) ghadan and ghadadan (as in kitab) and ghadadah (as in sahabah); so he is maghdub and ghadid": he restrained and lowered it, and it was said: it is when he brings his eyelids close together and looks. It was also said: al-ghadid is a glance with drooping eyelids. In the hadith: "When he was pleased, he lowered his glance," meaning he lowered and cast down his gaze and did not open his eyes wide. He did this so that he would be further from insolence and exultation. End quote. Ka'b and Kilab are two tribes of Tamim.]

* *

As for His words: ﴿those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for piety﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah are those whose hearts Allah has tested by putting them to the test, so He has chosen them and purified them for piety, meaning for guarding themselves against Him by performing His obedience and avoiding His disobedience, just as gold is tested by fire, so that its good quality is refined and its impurity is removed [[The pronoun in "jayyiduha" and "khabathuha" refers back to gold (al-dhahab), since it is feminine, and it may also be treated as masculine.]].

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿Allah has tested their hearts﴾, he said: "He purified them."

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿Allah has tested their hearts﴾, he said: "Allah purified their hearts in what He loves."

* *

As for His words: ﴿For them is forgiveness﴾

He says: For them there is pardon from Allah for their past sins, and remission from Him concerning them. ﴿And a great reward﴾, meaning: an abundant reward, which is Paradise.

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the private chambers—most of them do not reason.﴾ ﴿And if they had been patient until you came out to them, it would have been better for them. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

His exalted remembrance says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Indeed, those who call out to you, O Muhammad, from behind your chambers (ḥujurāt). The word ḥujurāt is the plural of ḥujra; its triptote plural is ḥujar, and then ḥujar is pluralised as ḥujurāt and ḥujarāt. Some of the Arabs pluralise ḥujr as ḥajarāt with an open jīm. Likewise, every plural of the pattern fu'al (of three to ten items) is pluralised by them as fa'alāt, with its second letter vocalised with a fatḥa; but the nominative (ḥujurāt, with ḍamma) is the more eloquent and preferable form. Among the evidence for this is the verse of the poet:

Was there not ʿAbbād, a peer (kafīʾ) to the Dārim,
Yes indeed, and for the houses in which are the ḥujurāt?

[[In al-Mubarrad's al-Kāmil (Ḥalabī edition, p. 85): it is said, "Fulān is the kafāʾ of Fulān," and "kafīʾ of Fulān," and "kafʾ of Fulān," meaning his equal. It is related that al-Farazdaq was informed that a man from the Ḥabiṭāt, sons of ʿAmr ibn Tamīm, had proposed to a woman from the Banū Dārim ibn Mālik ibn Ḥanẓala ibn Mālik ibn Zayd Manāt ibn Tamīm. Al-Farazdaq said:
"The Banū Dārim, their peers are the Āl Mismaʿ, and the Ḥabiṭāt marry into their peers."
(Āl Mismaʿ is the house of Bakr ibn Wāʾil in Islam, and they are of the Banū Qays ibn Thaʿlaba ibn ʿUkāba.) He said: then a man from the Ḥabiṭāt said: "Was not ʿAbbād a peer..." the verse, meaning the Banū Hāshim (he intends the houses of the Banū Hāshim), from the words of God, mighty and majestic: "Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the ḥujurāt." The evidence in the verse is his saying "ḥujurāt" with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and jīm, which is the plural of ḥujra; the ḥujra and its like are pluralised as ḥujurāt with two ḍammas, and with ḍamma then fatḥa, and with ḍamma then sukūn. The author holds that the first plural is more eloquent and preferable. End.]] He says: Yes, and for the Banū Hāshim.

It has been mentioned that this verse and the one after it were revealed concerning a group of Bedouins who came calling out to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from behind his chambers: "O Muhammad, come out to us."

Mention of the narrations to this effect:

◆ Abū ʿAmmār al-Marwazī and al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ḥārith told us, both said: al-Faḍl ibn Mūsā told us, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Wāqid, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Barāʾ, regarding His words "Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the ḥujurāt": he said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, indeed my praise is an adornment, and indeed my blame is a disgrace." The Prophet ﷺ said: "That is Allah, blessed and exalted."

◆ Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Wāḍiḥ told us, he said: al-Ḥusayn told us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Barāʾ, the like of it, except that he said: "That is Allah, mighty and majestic."

◆ al-Ḥasan ibn ʿArafa told us, he said: al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān al-Taymī told us, he said: I heard Dāwūd al-Ṭufāwī say: I heard Abū Muslim al-Bajalī narrate from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: Some people from the Arabs came to the Prophet ﷺ, and some of them said to others: "Let us go to this man; if he is a prophet, we are the happiest of people with him, and if he is a king, we will be honoured in his shade." He said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him of that. He said: Then they came to the chamber of the Prophet ﷺ and began calling out: "O Muhammad!" So Allah revealed to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the ḥujurāt—most of them do not reason.﴾ He said: The Messenger of Allah took my ear and pulled it, and began saying: "Allah has confirmed your statement, O Zayd, Allah has confirmed your statement, O Zayd."

◆ al-Ḥasan ibn Abī Yaḥyā al-Muqaddamī told us, he said: ʿAffān told us, he said: Wuhayb told us, he said: Mūsā ibn ʿUqba told us, from Abū Salama, who said: al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis al-Tamīmī narrated to me that he came to the Prophet ﷺ, called out to him and said: "O Muhammad, indeed my praise is an adornment, and indeed my reviling is a disgrace." The Prophet ﷺ came out to him and said: "Woe to you, that is Allah." Then Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the ḥujurāt⁠﴾ ... the verse.

◆ Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us, all from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding His words "Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the ḥujurāt": they are the Bedouins of Banū Tamīm.

◆ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and called out to him from behind the ḥujar, saying: "O Muhammad, indeed my praise is an adornment, and indeed my reviling is a disgrace." The Prophet ﷺ came out to him and said: "Woe to you, that is Allah." So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the ḥujurāt—most of them do not reason.﴾

◆ Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda, regarding His words "Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the ḥujurāt" ... the verse: it was mentioned to us that a man began calling, "O Prophet of Allah! O Muhammad!" The Prophet ﷺ came out to him and said: "What is your matter?" He said: "By Allah, indeed his praise is an adornment, and indeed his blame is a disgrace." The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "That is Allah." The man turned away. It was mentioned to us that the man was a poet.

◆ Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī ʿAmra, who said: Bishr ibn Ghālib and Labīd ibn ʿUṭārid—or Bishr ibn ʿUṭārid and Labīd ibn Ghālib—were sitting with al-Ḥajjāj, and Bishr ibn Ghālib said to Labīd ibn ʿUṭārid: "This verse was revealed concerning your people, the Banū Tamīm: ﴿Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the ḥujurāt⁠﴾." I mentioned that to Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and he said: "As for him, if he had known the end of the verse, he would have answered him: ﴿They consider it a favour to you that they have embraced Islam⁠﴾." They said: "We have embraced Islam, and the Banū Asad did not fight you."

◆ Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from al-Mubārak ibn Faḍāla, from al-Ḥasan, who said: "A Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ from behind his chambers and said: 'O Muhammad, O Muhammad!' The Prophet ﷺ came out to him and said: 'What is wrong with you? What is wrong with you?' He said: 'You know that my praise is an adornment, and that my blame is a disgrace.' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'That is Allah,' and then this was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet⁠﴾."

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words ﴿from behind the ḥujurāt⁠﴾. The readers of the cities recited it with a ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and the jīm, ḥujurāt, except Abū Jaʿfar al-Qārī, who recited it with a ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and a fatḥa on the jīm, according to what I have described, as the plural of ḥujra, ḥujar, and then the plural of ḥujr: ḥujurāt.

The correct recitation in our view is ḍamma on both letters, for the reason I described earlier.

* *

As for His words ﴿most of them do not reason⁠﴾:

He says: most of them are ignorant of the religion of Allah, and of what is incumbent upon them of your right and your honouring.

* *

As for His words ﴿And if they had been patient until you came out to them, it would have been better for them⁠﴾:

His exalted remembrance says: If these who call out to you, O Muhammad, from behind the chambers, had been patient and not called out until you came out to them when you emerged, it would have been better for them with Allah, because Allah has commanded them to revere and honour you, and by leaving off calling you they abandon what Allah has forbidden them. (﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful⁠﴾) His exalted remembrance says: Allah is Pardoning toward whoever calls out to you from behind the veil, if he repents from disobedience to Allah by calling you thus, and returns to the command of Allah in that and in other matters; Merciful to him, not punishing him for that sin after his repentance from it.

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the private chambers—most of them do not reason.﴾ ﴿And if they had been patient until you came out to them, it would have been better for them. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

The word ḥujurāt is the plural of ḥujra; its triptote plural is ḥujar, and then ḥujar is pluralised as ḥujurāt and ḥujarāt. Some of the Arabs pluralise ḥujr as ḥajarāt with an open jīm. Likewise, every plural of the pattern fu'al (of three to ten items) is pluralised by them as fa'alāt, with its second letter vocalised with a fatḥa; but the nominative (ḥujurāt, with ḍamma) is the more eloquent and preferable form. Among the evidence for this is the verse of the poet:

Was there not ʿAbbād, a peer (kafīʾ) to the Dārim,
Yes indeed, and for the houses in which are the ḥujurāt?

[[In al-Mubarrad's al-Kāmil (Ḥalabī edition, p. 85): it is said, "Fulān is the kafāʾ of Fulān," and "kafīʾ of Fulān," and "kafʾ of Fulān," meaning his equal. It is related that al-Farazdaq was informed that a man from the Ḥabiṭāt, sons of ʿAmr ibn Tamīm, had proposed to a woman from the Banū Dārim ibn Mālik ibn Ḥanẓala ibn Mālik ibn Zayd Manāt ibn Tamīm. Al-Farazdaq said:
"The Banū Dārim, their peers are the Āl Mismaʿ, and the Ḥabiṭāt marry into their peers."
(Āl Mismaʿ is the house of Bakr ibn Wāʾil in Islam, and they are of the Banū Qays ibn Thaʿlaba ibn ʿUkāba.) He said: then a man from the Ḥabiṭāt said: "Was not ʿAbbād a peer..." the verse, meaning the Banū Hāshim (he intends the houses of the Banū Hāshim), from the words of God, mighty and majestic: "Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the ḥujurāt." The evidence in the verse is his saying "ḥujurāt" with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and jīm, which is the plural of ḥujra; the ḥujra and its like are pluralised as ḥujurāt with two ḍammas, and with ḍamma then fatḥa, and with ḍamma then sukūn. It has been mentioned that this verse and the one after it were revealed concerning a group of Bedouins who came calling out to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from behind his chambers: "O Muhammad, come out to us."

Mention of the narrations to this effect:

◆ Abū ʿAmmār al-Marwazī and al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ḥārith told us, both said: al-Faḍl ibn Mūsā told us, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Wāqid, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Barāʾ, regarding His words "Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the ḥujurāt": he said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, indeed my praise is an adornment, and indeed my blame is a disgrace." The Prophet ﷺ said: "That is Allah, blessed and exalted."

◆ Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Wāḍiḥ told us, he said: al-Ḥusayn told us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Barāʾ, the like of it, except that he said: "That is Allah, mighty and majestic."

◆ al-Ḥasan ibn ʿArafa told us, he said: al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān al-Taymī told us, he said: I heard Dāwūd al-Ṭufāwī say: I heard Abū Muslim al-Bajalī narrate from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: Some people from the Arabs came to the Prophet ﷺ, and some of them said to others: "Let us go to this man; if he is a prophet, we are the happiest of people with him, and if he is a king, we will be honoured in his shade." He said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him of that. He said: Then they came to the chamber of the Prophet ﷺ and began calling out: "O Muhammad!" So Allah revealed to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the ḥujurāt—most of them do not reason.﴾ He said: The Messenger of Allah took my ear and pulled it, and began saying: "Allah has confirmed your statement, O Zayd, Allah has confirmed your statement, O Zayd."

◆ al-Ḥasan ibn Abī Yaḥyā al-Muqaddamī told us, he said: ʿAffān told us, he said: Wuhayb told us, he said: Mūsā ibn ʿUqba told us, from Abū Salama, who said: al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis al-Tamīmī narrated to me that he came to the Prophet ﷺ, called out to him and said: "O Muhammad, indeed my praise is an adornment, and indeed my reviling is a disgrace." The Prophet ﷺ came out to him and said: "Woe to you, that is Allah." Then Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the ḥujurāt⁠﴾ ... the verse.

◆ Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us, all from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding His words "Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the ḥujurāt": they are the Bedouins of Banū Tamīm.

◆ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and called out to him from behind the ḥujar, saying: "O Muhammad, indeed my praise is an adornment, and indeed my reviling is a disgrace." The Prophet ﷺ came out to him and said: "Woe to you, that is Allah." So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the ḥujurāt—most of them do not reason.﴾

◆ Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda, regarding His words "Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the ḥujurāt" ... the verse: it was mentioned to us that a man began calling, "O Prophet of Allah! O Muhammad!" The Prophet ﷺ came out to him and said: "What is your matter?" He said: "By Allah, indeed his praise is an adornment, and indeed his blame is a disgrace." The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "That is Allah." The man turned away. It was mentioned to us that the man was a poet.

◆ Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī ʿAmra, who said: Bishr ibn Ghālib and Labīd ibn ʿUṭārid—or Bishr ibn ʿUṭārid and Labīd ibn Ghālib—were sitting with al-Ḥajjāj, and Bishr ibn Ghālib said to Labīd ibn ʿUṭārid: "This verse was revealed concerning your people, the Banū Tamīm: ﴿Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the ḥujurāt⁠﴾." The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words ﴿from behind the ḥujurāt⁠﴾. The readers of the cities recited it with a ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and the jīm, ḥujurāt, except Abū Jaʿfar al-Qārī, who recited it with a ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and a fatḥa on the jīm, according to what I have described, as the plural of ḥujra, ḥujar, and then the plural of ḥujr: ḥujurāt.

The correct recitation in our view is ḍamma on both letters, for the reason I described earlier.

* *

As for His words ﴿most of them do not reason⁠﴾:

He says: most of them are ignorant of the religion of Allah, and of what is incumbent upon them of your right and your honouring.

* *

As for His words ﴿And if they had been patient until you came out to them, it would have been better for them⁠﴾:

His exalted remembrance says: If these who call out to you, O Muhammad, from behind the chambers, had been patient and not called out until you came out to them when you emerged, it would have been better for them with Allah, because Allah has commanded them to revere and honour you, and by leaving off calling you they abandon what Allah has forbidden them. (﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful⁠﴾) His exalted remembrance says: Allah is Pardoning toward whoever calls out to you from behind the veil, if he repents from disobedience to Allah by calling you thus, and returns to the command of Allah in that and in other matters; Merciful to him, not punishing him for that sin after his repentance from it.

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, if there comes to you a deviator with information, investigate, lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful.﴾ (6)

He, the Exalted, says: O you who have affirmed Allah and His Messenger, ﴿if there comes to you a deviator with information﴾ about a people, ﴿then investigate﴾.

The readers differed over the recitation of His saying ﴿fa-tabayyanu﴾. The majority of the readers of Madinah recited ﴿fa-tathabbatu﴾ with the letter thā’ (ث), and it is reported that in the Codex of Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) it is pointed with the thā’. Some readers recited ﴿fa-tabayyanu﴾ with the letter bā’ (ب), meaning: wait until you know its soundness; do not hasten to accept it. The meaning of ﴿fa-tathabbatu﴾ is likewise.

The correct view on this is that they are two well-known recitations, close in meaning, and whichever of them the reader recites is correct.

It is reported that this verse was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt.

Mention of the occasion for which this was said:

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Awn related to us, from Musa ibn Ubaydah, from Thabit, the client of Umm Salamah, from Umm Salamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a man to collect the sadaqat (alms) of Bani al-Mustaliq after the battle. The people heard of this and went out to meet him, honouring the matter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: Then Satan whispered to him that they intended to kill him. She said: So he returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: Bani al-Mustaliq have withheld their sadaqat. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims became angry. He said: When the people learned of his return, they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and, after the Dhuhr prayer, presented themselves before him, saying: We seek refuge in Allah from the wrath of Allah and the wrath of His Messenger. You sent to us a collector, and we rejoiced at that and our eyes were gladdened. Then he returned from part of the way, and we feared that this was anger from Allah and from His Messenger. They did not cease speaking to him until Bilal came and called the adhan for the ʿAsr prayer. He said: And there was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, if there comes to you a deviator with information, investigate, lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful.﴾

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Humayd, from Hilal al-Ansari, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, concerning ﴿if there comes to you a deviator with information﴾, he said: It was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn Uqbah when he was sent to Bani al-Mustaliq.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿O you who have believed, if there comes to you a deviator with information﴾ ... to the end of the verse, he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had sent al-Walid ibn Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt, then a man of Bani Amr ibn Umayyah, then a man of Bani Abi Mu'ayt, to Bani al-Mustaliq to take the sadaqat from them. When the news reached them, they rejoiced and went out to meet the messenger of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When al-Walid reported that they had come out to meet him, he returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of Allah, Bani al-Mustaliq have withheld the sadaqah. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) became exceedingly angry. While he was reflecting on whether to raid them, the delegation came to him and said: O Messenger of Allah, we were told that your messenger turned back from halfway along the road, and we feared that what turned him back was a letter he received from you because of anger you felt toward us. We seek refuge in Allah from His anger and the anger of His Messenger. So Allah sent down their excuse in the Book, saying: ﴿O you who have believed, if there comes to you a deviator with information, investigate, lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful.﴾

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿if there comes to you a deviator with information﴾, he said: It is al-Walid ibn Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt, whom the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) sent to Bani al-Mustaliq to collect their sadaqah. They met him with gifts, but he returned to Muhammad (ﷺ) and said: Bani al-Mustaliq have gathered to fight you.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿O you who have believed, if there comes to you a deviator with information﴾ ... up to ﴿out of ignorance﴾: he is Ibn Abi Mu'ayt, al-Walid ibn Uqbah, whom the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) sent as a collector to Bani al-Mustaliq. When they saw him, they came toward him, and he feared them, so he returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him that they had apostatized from Islam. The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) sent Khalid ibn al-Walid and ordered him to verify and not to hasten. He set out until he came to them at night and sent his scouts. When they came back, they informed Khalid that they were holding firmly to Islam, and they heard their adhan and their prayer. When morning came, Khalid went to them and saw what pleased him. He returned to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him of the news, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed what you have heard. The Prophet of Allah used to say: Verification is from Allah, and haste is from Satan.

Ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿O you who have believed, if there comes to you a deviator with information﴾, and he related something similar.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Hilal al-Wazzan, from Ibn Abi Layla, concerning His saying ﴿O you who have believed, if there comes to you a deviator with information, then investigate﴾, he said: It was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt.

Salamah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to us, from Yazid ibn Ruman, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent al-Walid ibn Abi Mu'ayt to Bani al-Mustaliq after their conversion to Islam. When they heard of him, they rode out to him. When he saw them he feared them and returned to the Messenger of Allah, and informed him that the people had resolved to kill him and had withheld what was due from them of their sadaqat. The Muslims spoke much about raiding them, until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) resolved to raid them. While they were in that state, their delegation came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of Allah, we heard of your messenger when you sent him to us, so we went out to him to honour him and to pay him what was due from us of the sadaqah. Then he continued returning, and we learned that he claimed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that we went out to him to fight him, and by Allah, we did not go out for that. So Allah revealed concerning al-Walid ibn Uqbah and them: ﴿O you who have believed, if there comes to you a deviator with information﴾ ... the verse.

He said: [[It appears that this is the beginning of another narration, which he cited in al-Durr from Jabir.]] The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a man from among his companions to a people to collect their sadaqah. The man came to them, and there had been a previous enmity between him and them in the Jahiliyyah. When he came to them, they welcomed him, acknowledged the zakat, and gave what was due from them. The man returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of Allah, such-and-such people have withheld the sadaqah and have turned back from Islam. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) became angry and sent to them. They came to him, and he said: Did you withhold the zakah and drive away my messenger? They said: By Allah, we did not do that; we know that you are the Messenger of Allah, and we have no excuse, and we have not withheld Allah's right in our wealth. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not accept their word, so Allah revealed this verse, and thereby excused them.

* *

As for His saying ﴿lest you harm a people out of ignorance﴾:

He, the Exalted, says: Investigate, lest you harm people who are innocent of what they have been accused of, through a crime committed by you out of ignorance. ﴿And become, over what you have done, regretful﴾: that is, you will regret harming them with the wrong you would inflict upon them.

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He:

﴿And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would surely be in difficulty. But Allah has endeared to you faith and has made it attractive in your hearts, and has made disbelief, defiance, and disobedience hateful to you. Those are the ones who are rightly guided. [It is] a bounty from Allah and favor. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the companions of the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ): "And know, O believers in Allah and His Messenger, that among you is the Messenger of Allah. So fear Allah, lest you say falsehood and invent lies, for Allah informs him of your affairs, makes known to him your news, and sets him right in his affairs."

* *

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: If the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were to act in affairs according to your opinions and accept from you what you say to him, and obey you, ﴿you would surely be in difficulty﴾. He says: you would encounter hardship (ʿanat), meaning severity and distress, in many matters through his obeying you, if he obeyed you, because he would err in his actions. Like if he had accepted the statement of al-Walid ibn ʿUqba concerning the Banu al-Mustaliq, that they had apostatized, withheld the zakat, and gathered forces to raid the Muslims, and he (the Prophet) had marched against them and killed some of them and taken some of their blood and property, then he would have killed those whom it was not lawful for him or for you to kill, and he and you would have taken property that was not lawful for him or for you to take from the wealth of a Muslim people. Hardship from Allah would have befallen you because of that. ﴿But Allah has endeared to you faith﴾ in Allah and His Messenger. So you obey the Messenger of Allah and follow him, and Allah protects you by that from the hardship which would have reached and afflicted you had you not obeyed and followed him, and had he obeyed you.

Disobedience is disobedience to the Prophet (ﷺ)." [He said:] ﴿Those are the ones who are rightly guided﴾: "From where did this come?" He said: "A bounty from Allah and favor." He said: "Allah has named the hypocrites all together in the Qur'an as liars." He said: "And the fasiq (defiant one) is the liar in the whole Book of Allah."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 49, verse 9:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight, then make peace between them. But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight against the one that oppresses until it returns to the command of Allah. And if it returns, then make peace between them with justice and act equitably. Indeed, Allah loves those who act equitably.﴾ (49:9)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And if two groups from among the people of faith fight, then make peace between them, O believers, by calling them to the judgment of the Book of Allah and by their acceptance of what it contains for them and against them. That is the reconciliation between them with justice. ﴿But if one of them oppresses the other﴾ means: if one of these two groups refuses to comply with the judgment of the Book of Allah, whether in its favour or against it, and transgresses what Allah has made a just standard among His creation, while the other group complies. ﴿Then fight against the one that oppresses﴾ means: fight the group that transgresses and refuses to comply with the judgment of Allah. ﴿Until it returns to the command of Allah﴾ means: until it returns to the judgment of Allah which He has decreed in His Book among His creation. ﴿And if it returns, then make peace between them with justice﴾ means: if the oppressing group, after your fighting against them, returns to acceptance of the judgment of Allah in His Book, then make peace between it and the other group you fought against, with justice, that is, with equity between them. That is the judgment of Allah in His Book, which He made a just standard among His creation.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight, then make peace between them. But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight against the one that oppresses until it returns to the command of Allah.﴾ He said: Allah, glorified is He, commanded the Prophet ﷺ and the believers that when two groups of the believers fight, they should call them to the judgment of Allah and bring about equity between them. If they respond, judgment is given among them by the Book of Allah, until the wronged is given equity against the wrongdoer. Whoever among them refuses to respond is a transgressor, and it is incumbent upon the imam of the believers to strive against them and fight them until they return to the command of Allah and acknowledge the judgment of Allah.

* Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight﴾ ... to the end of the verse. He said: This is a command from Allah which He directed to the rulers, similar to what occurs when a faction arises among people, and He commanded them to make peace between them. If they refuse, they should fight the transgressing faction until it returns to the command of Allah. When it returns, they should make peace between them, and inform them that the believers are brothers, so make peace between your two brothers. He said: And none fights the transgressing faction except the imam.

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning two groups of the Aws and the Khazraj who fought over some matter in which they disputed, which I will mention, God willing, exalted is He.

Mention of the narration to that effect:

* Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, he said: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, from Anas, who said: It was said to the Prophet ﷺ: "If only you would go to Abd Allah ibn Ubayy." He said: So he set out to him, mounted a donkey, and the Muslims set out with him, and it was a salty land. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached him, he said: "Stay away from me, for by Allah, the stench of your donkey has harmed me." A man from the Ansar said: "By Allah, the donkey of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has a more pleasant scent than you." He said: A man from the people of Abd Allah ibn Ubayy became angry for him. He said: Then each of the two men's companions became angry for him. He said: There was then a striking with palm stalks, hands and sandals among them. It has reached us that this verse was revealed concerning them: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight, then make peace between them.﴾

* Abu Husayn Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to me, he said: Abthar narrated to us, he said: Husayn narrated to me, from Abu Malik regarding His saying: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight, then make peace between them.﴾ He said: Two men fought, and each one's tribe became angry for him, and they gathered until they struck one another with sandals, until fighting almost occurred between them, so Allah revealed this verse.

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Husayn, from Abu Malik, regarding His saying: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight﴾ He said: There was fighting among them without weapons.

* Ya'qub narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, he said: Husayn informed us, from Abu Malik, regarding His saying: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight, then make peace between them.﴾ He said: They were two clans of the clans of the Ansar, and there was a dispute between them without weapons.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir informed us, from Mansur, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight, then make peace between them.﴾ He said: Their fighting was with sandals and staves, so He commanded them to make peace between them.

* He said: Mihran narrated to us, he said: al-Mubarak ibn Fadala narrated to us, from al-Hasan: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight﴾ He said: There would be a dispute between two clans, and he would call them to judgment, and they would refuse to respond, so Allah revealed: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight, then make peace between them. But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight against the one that oppresses until it returns to the command of Allah.﴾ He said: Call them to judgment; their fighting was the pushing.

* He said: Mihran narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight, then make peace between them.﴾ He said: There was a woman from the Ansar called Umm Zayd, who was married to a man, and there was something between her and her husband. He sent her up to an upper room and said to them: "Keep watch." This reached her people, and they came, and his people came, and they fought with hands and sandals. This reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he came to make peace between them, and the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight, then make peace between them. But if one of them oppresses the other﴾ He said: "Oppresses" means: does not accept the reconciliation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, or the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight﴾ He said: The Aws and the Khazraj fought with staves among themselves.

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight﴾ ... the verse. It has been mentioned to us that it was revealed concerning two men of the Ansar who had a dispute over a right between them. One of them said to the other: "I will take it from you by force, because of the multitude of my kinsmen." The other called him to be judged before the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, but he refused to follow him. The matter continued until they pushed one another, and until some of them grasped others with hands and sandals, and there was no fighting with swords. So Allah commanded that they be fought until they return to the command of Allah, the Book of Allah, and to the judgment of His Prophet ﷺ. It is not as those interpreted it, the people of doubts, the people of innovation, and the people of slander against Allah and His Book, who say that it refers to a believer whose killing is lawful for you. By Allah, Allah has magnified the sanctity of the believer, to the point that He forbade you to think ill of your brother except with good. He said: ﴿The believers are but brothers﴾ ... the verse.

* Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, that a people among the Muslims had a dispute between them until they struck one another with sandals and hands, so Allah revealed concerning them: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight﴾ Qatada said: There were two men between whom there was a right, and they disputed over it. One of them said: "I will take it by force, because of the multitude of my kinsmen." The other said: "Between me and you is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." They disputed until there was striking between them with sandals and hands.

* Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: Ibn Abbas narrated to me, he said: Zayd said, regarding the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight, then make peace between them﴾ — this refers to two men fighting from among the people of Islam, or a group and a group, or a tribe and a tribe. So Allah commanded the imams of the Muslims to judge between them by the truth which He revealed in His Book: either retaliation (qisas) and requital, or blood-money (diya) and camels, or pardon. ﴿But if one of them oppresses the other﴾ after that, the Muslims were to stand with the wronged against the wrongdoer, until it returns to the command of Allah and is content with it.

* Ibn al-Barqi narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, he said: Nafi' ibn Yazid informed us, he said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: Ibn Shihab and others narrated to me, some of them adding to the report of others, he said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat in a gathering in which was Abd Allah ibn Rawaha and Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left, Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul said: 'He has harmed us with the urine of his donkey, and stifled our breath.' There had been something between him and Ibn Rawaha, until they came out with weapons. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to them and separated them. For this reason Abd Allah ibn Ubayy says:

"Whenever your patron is your adversary, striving, you will be wronged, and those you wrestle will throw you down."

He said: So this verse was revealed concerning them: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight﴾.

* * *

As for His saying ﴿and act equitably﴾:

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And act justly, O believers, in your judgment between those among whom you judge, by not exceeding in your rulings the judgment of Allah and the judgment of His Messenger. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who act equitably﴾ means: Indeed, Allah loves those who are just in their judgments, who judge among His creation with equity.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 49, verse 10–11:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the believers are but brothers, so make reconciliation between your two brothers. And fear Allah that you may receive mercy.﴾ (10)

God, mentioned be He, says to the people of faith in Him: ﴿Indeed, the believers are but brothers﴾ in religion. ﴿So make reconciliation between your two brothers﴾ if they fight, by referring them to the judgement of Allah and the judgement of His Messenger. The meaning of "the two brothers" in this place is: every two fighting parties among the people of faith. The dual form is how the reciters of the major cities read it. It is reported from Ibn Sirin that he recited "between your brothers" with the nun, in the plural form; this is grammatically sound, but it contradicts what the reciters of the major cities follow, so I do not favour reciting it that way. ﴿And fear Allah that you may receive mercy﴾: God, mentioned be He, says: Fear Allah, O people, by performing His obligations upon you in reconciling the fighting parties among the people of faith with justice, and in His other obligations, and by avoiding His disobediences, so that your Lord may have mercy on you, and pardon you for your past transgressions if you obey Him, follow His command and prohibition, and fear Him by obeying Him.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O you who believe, let not a people ridicule [another] people, perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women, perhaps they may be better than them. And do not defame one another, nor call each other by nicknames. Wretched is the name of disobedience after faith. And whoever does not repent, then it is those who are the wrongdoers.﴾ (11)

God, mentioned be He, says: O you who believe in Allah and His Messenger, let not a believing people ridicule a believing people ﴿perhaps they may be better than them﴾; that is, the one ridiculed may be better than the ridiculers. ﴿Nor women [ridicule] women﴾; that is, let believing women not ridicule believing women, for the one ridiculed among them may be better than the ridiculers.

The people of interpretation differed concerning the mockery which God forbade the believers in this verse. Some of them said: it is the mockery of the rich toward the poor; it was forbidden to mock the poor for their poverty.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿let not a people ridicule [another] people﴾: he said: let not one people mock another by a man asking a rich man, or a poor man, or if a man bestows something upon him, he should not mock him for it.

Others said: rather, it is a prohibition from God, addressed to whoever among the people of faith has had his concealed fault covered, against mocking one whose fault has been exposed in this world.

Those who said that:

Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning ﴿O you who believe, let not a people ridicule [another] people, perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women, perhaps they may be better than them﴾: he said: a person may often stumble in his sin, perhaps they may be better than them, even though this stumble of his has become apparent while you have covered your own stumble. Perhaps what has been made apparent is better for him in the Hereafter with Allah, and what you have covered for yourself is worse for you; who knows, perhaps He will forgive you. He said: So the man was forbidden from that, and it was said: ﴿let not a people ridicule [another] people, perhaps they may be better than them﴾, and it said the same about women.

The correct view on this, in my opinion, is to say: by His prohibition to the believers that some of them ridicule others, God has encompassed all the meanings of mockery; it is not lawful for a believer to mock a believer, neither for his poverty, nor for a sin he committed, nor for anything else.

* *

And His saying: ﴿nor defame one another﴾

God, mentioned be He, says: Let none of you backbite another, O believers, and let none of you slander another. He said ﴿nor defame one another﴾, making the one who defames his brother a defamer of himself, because the believers are like one man in what binds them to one another: improving each other's condition, seeking each other's welfare, and loving good for one another. For this reason it is related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "The believers, in their mutual love, mercy and compassion, are like one body: when one limb complains, the rest of the body responds to it with wakefulness and fever." This is similar to His saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly, except through trade by mutual consent, and do not kill yourselves﴾, meaning: none of you should kill another.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this meaning.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿nor defame one another﴾: he said: do not find fault.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿nor defame one another﴾: he said: none of you should find fault with another.

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Mu'ammar, from Qatada, the like of it.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: my father told me, saying: my paternal uncle told me, saying: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿nor defame one another﴾: he said: none of you should find fault with another.

* *

His saying: ﴿nor call each other by nicknames﴾

That is: do not call one another by nicknames. Al-nabz and al-laqab have the same meaning; the plural of nabz is anbaz, and of laqab is alqab.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the nicknames which God forbade calling one another by in this verse. Some of them said: it refers to the nicknames by which the one so named dislikes being called. They said: this verse was revealed concerning a people who had names in the pre-Islamic period; when they embraced Islam, they were forbidden to call one another by the names they disliked, which they had been called by in the time of ignorance.

Those who said that:

Humayd ibn Mas'ada related to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Dawud related to us, from Amir, who said: Abu Jubayra ibn al-Dahhak said: "This verse was revealed about us, the Banu Salama. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came, and there was not a man among us but he had two or three names. When he called a man by one of the names, we would say: 'O Messenger of Allah, he becomes angry at this.' So this verse was revealed: ﴿nor call each other by nicknames﴾ ... the whole verse."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abd al-Wahhab related to us, saying: Dawud related to us, from Amir, from Abu Jubayra ibn al-Dahhak, who said: The people of the Jahiliyya used to name a man with names, and the Prophet (ﷺ) called a man by one of those names, so they said: "O Messenger of Allah, he becomes angry at this." So Allah revealed ﴿nor call each other by nicknames. Wretched is the name of disobedience after faith﴾.

Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Dawud related to us, from Amir, who said: Abu Jubayra ibn al-Dahhak told me, and he related from the Prophet (ﷺ), the like of it.

Yaqub told me, saying: Ibn Ulayya related to us, saying: Dawud informed us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Abu Jubayra ibn al-Dahhak told me, who said: "It was revealed concerning the Banu Salama: ﴿nor call each other by nicknames﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came, and there was not a man among us but he had two or three names; he would call a man, and his mother would say: 'He becomes angry at this.' So ﴿nor call each other by nicknames﴾ was revealed." And on one occasion he said: "When he called someone by one of these names, it was said: 'O Messenger of Allah, he becomes angry at this,' and the verse was revealed."

Others said: rather, it refers to a Muslim man calling another Muslim man: "O sinner! O adulterer!"

Those who said that:

Hannad ibn al-Sarri related to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Husayn, who said: I asked Ikrima about the saying of God ﴿nor call each other by nicknames﴾, and he said: It is a man saying to another: "O hypocrite! O unbeliever!"

Yaqub ibn Ibrahim related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Ikrima, regarding His saying ﴿nor call each other by nicknames﴾: he said: It is a man saying to another: "O sinner! O hypocrite!"

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Husayn, from Ikrima, regarding ﴿nor call each other by nicknames﴾: he said: "O sinner! O unbeliever!"

He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from Mujahid or Ikrima, regarding ﴿nor call each other by nicknames﴾: he said: a man says to another: "O sinner! O unbeliever!"

Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿nor call each other by nicknames﴾: he said: A man was called "unbeliever" while he was a Muslim.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿nor call each other by nicknames﴾: a man says: "Do not say to your Muslim brother: that one is a sinner, that one is a hypocrite." God forbade the Muslim from that and warned against it.

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Mu'ammar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿nor call each other by nicknames﴾: he says: let no one say to his Muslim brother: "O sinner! O hypocrite!"

Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding ﴿nor call each other by nicknames﴾: naming him by evil deeds after Islam: "adulterer, sinner."

Others said: rather, it refers to calling a man by unbelief after Islam, and by wickedness and ugly deeds after repentance.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: my father told me, saying: my paternal uncle told me, saying: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿nor call each other by nicknames. Wretched is the name of disobedience after faith﴾ ... the verse, he said: Calling one another by nicknames is when a man has committed evil deeds, then repents from them and returns to the truth, and God forbade reproaching him for what he had done before.

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Mu'ammar, who said: Al-Hasan said: a Jew or a Christian would embrace Islam, and then he would be given a nickname and be told: "O Jew! O Christian!" So they were forbidden from that.

The most preferable of these interpretations in my view, and the most correct, is to say: God, mentioned be He, forbade the believers to call one another by nicknames. Calling one another by nicknames is a person calling his companion by a name or attribute he dislikes. God prohibited this in general and did not single out some nicknames over others, so it is not permissible for any Muslim to call his brother by a name or attribute he dislikes. Given this, the views the people of interpretation stated on this matter, which we have mentioned, are all correct, and none of them is more correct than another, since all of them are things God forbade the Muslims from, one calling another by.

* *

His saying: ﴿Wretched is the name of disobedience after faith﴾

God, mentioned be He, says: Whoever does what we have been forbidden, and transgresses our disobedience after his faith, by mocking the believers, defaming his believing brother, and calling him by nicknames, is a sinner. ﴿Wretched is the name of disobedience after faith﴾: that is, do not do so, lest if you do it you deserve to be named sinners; wretched is the name of disobedience. The mention of what we have described has been omitted, being sufficiently indicated by His saying ﴿wretched is the name of disobedience﴾.

Ibn Zayd used to say about this:

Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, and recited ﴿Wretched is the name of disobedience after faith﴾: "Wretched is the name of disobedience when you name him with sinfulness after Islam, while he is upon Islam." He said: The people of this opinion are the Mu'tazila. They said: "We do not declare him a disbeliever as the people of innovation declare him, nor do we say he is a believer as the community says; rather we name him by his name: if he is a thief, we call him a thief; if he is treacherous, we call him treacherous; if he is an adulterer, we call him an adulterer." He said: So they withdrew from both groups, the people of innovation and the people of the community, so they did not adopt the view of either, and so they were named Mu'tazila.

Ibn Zayd's interpretation of His saying ﴿Wretched is the name of disobedience after faith﴾ refers to one who is called a sinner while he has repented of his sin; so that name is wretched for him among his names... Another interpretation is more fitting to the discourse, because God began this verse by forbidding what He forbade, so it is more fitting to conclude it with a threat against whoever transgresses His prohibitions, or against the ugliness of what he committed of what was forbidden, rather than to inform about the ugliness of what the repentant one did before his repentance, given that the verse did not open with a report of his committing the ugliness he had committed before repentance, so that its end would be a threat for it or a statement of its ugliness.

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever does not repent, then it is those who are the wrongdoers﴾

God, mentioned be He, says: Whoever does not repent from defaming his brother with the nicknames God forbade, or from reproaching him, or from mocking him, then those are the ones who wronged themselves, bringing upon themselves God's punishment by committing what He forbade them.

Ibn Zayd used to say about this:

Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding ﴿And whoever does not repent, then it is those who are the wrongdoers﴾: he said: whoever does not repent from that sinfulness, then those are the wrongdoers.
