The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O you who believe, let not a people ridicule [another] people, perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women, perhaps they may be better than them. And do not defame one another, nor call each other by nicknames. Wretched is the name of disobedience after faith. And whoever does not repent, then it is those who are the wrongdoers.﴾ (11)

God, mentioned be He, says: O you who believe in Allah and His Messenger, let not a believing people ridicule a believing people ﴿perhaps they may be better than them﴾; that is, the one ridiculed may be better than the ridiculers. ﴿Nor women [ridicule] women﴾; that is, let believing women not ridicule believing women, for the one ridiculed among them may be better than the ridiculers.

The people of interpretation differed concerning the mockery which God forbade the believers in this verse. Some of them said: it is the mockery of the rich toward the poor; it was forbidden to mock the poor for their poverty.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿let not a people ridicule [another] people﴾: he said: let not one people mock another by a man asking a rich man, or a poor man, or if a man bestows something upon him, he should not mock him for it.

Others said: rather, it is a prohibition from God, addressed to whoever among the people of faith has had his concealed fault covered, against mocking one whose fault has been exposed in this world.

Those who said that:

Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning ﴿O you who believe, let not a people ridicule [another] people, perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women, perhaps they may be better than them﴾: he said: a person may often stumble in his sin, perhaps they may be better than them, even though this stumble of his has become apparent while you have covered your own stumble. Perhaps what has been made apparent is better for him in the Hereafter with Allah, and what you have covered for yourself is worse for you; who knows, perhaps He will forgive you. He said: So the man was forbidden from that, and it was said: ﴿let not a people ridicule [another] people, perhaps they may be better than them﴾, and it said the same about women.

The correct view on this, in my opinion, is to say: by His prohibition to the believers that some of them ridicule others, God has encompassed all the meanings of mockery; it is not lawful for a believer to mock a believer, neither for his poverty, nor for a sin he committed, nor for anything else.

* *

And His saying: ﴿nor defame one another﴾

God, mentioned be He, says: Let none of you backbite another, O believers, and let none of you slander another. He said ﴿nor defame one another﴾, making the one who defames his brother a defamer of himself, because the believers are like one man in what binds them to one another: improving each other's condition, seeking each other's welfare, and loving good for one another. For this reason it is related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "The believers, in their mutual love, mercy and compassion, are like one body: when one limb complains, the rest of the body responds to it with wakefulness and fever." This is similar to His saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly, except through trade by mutual consent, and do not kill yourselves﴾, meaning: none of you should kill another.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this meaning.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿nor defame one another﴾: he said: do not find fault.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿nor defame one another﴾: he said: none of you should find fault with another.

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Mu'ammar, from Qatada, the like of it.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: my father told me, saying: my paternal uncle told me, saying: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿nor defame one another﴾: he said: none of you should find fault with another.

* *

His saying: ﴿nor call each other by nicknames﴾

That is: do not call one another by nicknames. Al-nabz and al-laqab have the same meaning; the plural of nabz is anbaz, and of laqab is alqab.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the nicknames which God forbade calling one another by in this verse. Some of them said: it refers to the nicknames by which the one so named dislikes being called. They said: this verse was revealed concerning a people who had names in the pre-Islamic period; when they embraced Islam, they were forbidden to call one another by the names they disliked, which they had been called by in the time of ignorance.

Those who said that:

Humayd ibn Mas'ada related to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Dawud related to us, from Amir, who said: Abu Jubayra ibn al-Dahhak said: "This verse was revealed about us, the Banu Salama. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came, and there was not a man among us but he had two or three names. When he called a man by one of the names, we would say: 'O Messenger of Allah, he becomes angry at this.' So this verse was revealed: ﴿nor call each other by nicknames﴾ ... the whole verse."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abd al-Wahhab related to us, saying: Dawud related to us, from Amir, from Abu Jubayra ibn al-Dahhak, who said: The people of the Jahiliyya used to name a man with names, and the Prophet (ﷺ) called a man by one of those names, so they said: "O Messenger of Allah, he becomes angry at this." So Allah revealed ﴿nor call each other by nicknames. Wretched is the name of disobedience after faith﴾.

Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Dawud related to us, from Amir, who said: Abu Jubayra ibn al-Dahhak told me, and he related from the Prophet (ﷺ), the like of it.

Yaqub told me, saying: Ibn Ulayya related to us, saying: Dawud informed us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Abu Jubayra ibn al-Dahhak told me, who said: "It was revealed concerning the Banu Salama: ﴿nor call each other by nicknames﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came, and there was not a man among us but he had two or three names; he would call a man, and his mother would say: 'He becomes angry at this.' So ﴿nor call each other by nicknames﴾ was revealed." And on one occasion he said: "When he called someone by one of these names, it was said: 'O Messenger of Allah, he becomes angry at this,' and the verse was revealed."

Others said: rather, it refers to a Muslim man calling another Muslim man: "O sinner! O adulterer!"

Those who said that:

Hannad ibn al-Sarri related to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Husayn, who said: I asked Ikrima about the saying of God ﴿nor call each other by nicknames﴾, and he said: It is a man saying to another: "O hypocrite! O unbeliever!"

Yaqub ibn Ibrahim related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Ikrima, regarding His saying ﴿nor call each other by nicknames﴾: he said: It is a man saying to another: "O sinner! O hypocrite!"

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Husayn, from Ikrima, regarding ﴿nor call each other by nicknames﴾: he said: "O sinner! O unbeliever!"

He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from Mujahid or Ikrima, regarding ﴿nor call each other by nicknames﴾: he said: a man says to another: "O sinner! O unbeliever!"

Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿nor call each other by nicknames﴾: he said: A man was called "unbeliever" while he was a Muslim.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿nor call each other by nicknames﴾: a man says: "Do not say to your Muslim brother: that one is a sinner, that one is a hypocrite." God forbade the Muslim from that and warned against it.

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Mu'ammar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿nor call each other by nicknames﴾: he says: let no one say to his Muslim brother: "O sinner! O hypocrite!"

Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding ﴿nor call each other by nicknames﴾: naming him by evil deeds after Islam: "adulterer, sinner."

Others said: rather, it refers to calling a man by unbelief after Islam, and by wickedness and ugly deeds after repentance.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: my father told me, saying: my paternal uncle told me, saying: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿nor call each other by nicknames. Wretched is the name of disobedience after faith﴾ ... the verse, he said: Calling one another by nicknames is when a man has committed evil deeds, then repents from them and returns to the truth, and God forbade reproaching him for what he had done before.

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Mu'ammar, who said: Al-Hasan said: a Jew or a Christian would embrace Islam, and then he would be given a nickname and be told: "O Jew! O Christian!" So they were forbidden from that.

The most preferable of these interpretations in my view, and the most correct, is to say: God, mentioned be He, forbade the believers to call one another by nicknames. Calling one another by nicknames is a person calling his companion by a name or attribute he dislikes. God prohibited this in general and did not single out some nicknames over others, so it is not permissible for any Muslim to call his brother by a name or attribute he dislikes. Given this, the views the people of interpretation stated on this matter, which we have mentioned, are all correct, and none of them is more correct than another, since all of them are things God forbade the Muslims from, one calling another by.

* *

His saying: ﴿Wretched is the name of disobedience after faith﴾

God, mentioned be He, says: Whoever does what we have been forbidden, and transgresses our disobedience after his faith, by mocking the believers, defaming his believing brother, and calling him by nicknames, is a sinner. ﴿Wretched is the name of disobedience after faith﴾: that is, do not do so, lest if you do it you deserve to be named sinners; wretched is the name of disobedience. The mention of what we have described has been omitted, being sufficiently indicated by His saying ﴿wretched is the name of disobedience﴾.

Ibn Zayd used to say about this:

Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, and recited ﴿Wretched is the name of disobedience after faith﴾: "Wretched is the name of disobedience when you name him with sinfulness after Islam, while he is upon Islam." He said: The people of this opinion are the Mu'tazila. They said: "We do not declare him a disbeliever as the people of innovation declare him, nor do we say he is a believer as the community says; rather we name him by his name: if he is a thief, we call him a thief; if he is treacherous, we call him treacherous; if he is an adulterer, we call him an adulterer." He said: So they withdrew from both groups, the people of innovation and the people of the community, so they did not adopt the view of either, and so they were named Mu'tazila.

Ibn Zayd's interpretation of His saying ﴿Wretched is the name of disobedience after faith﴾ refers to one who is called a sinner while he has repented of his sin; so that name is wretched for him among his names... Another interpretation is more fitting to the discourse, because God began this verse by forbidding what He forbade, so it is more fitting to conclude it with a threat against whoever transgresses His prohibitions, or against the ugliness of what he committed of what was forbidden, rather than to inform about the ugliness of what the repentant one did before his repentance, given that the verse did not open with a report of his committing the ugliness he had committed before repentance, so that its end would be a threat for it or a statement of its ugliness.

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever does not repent, then it is those who are the wrongdoers﴾

God, mentioned be He, says: Whoever does not repent from defaming his brother with the nicknames God forbade, or from reproaching him, or from mocking him, then those are the ones who wronged themselves, bringing upon themselves God's punishment by committing what He forbade them.

Ibn Zayd used to say about this:

Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding ﴿And whoever does not repent, then it is those who are the wrongdoers﴾: he said: whoever does not repent from that sinfulness, then those are the wrongdoers.

Al-Tabari, *Jami' al-Bayan*, commentary on Surah 49, verse 12:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, avoid much of [negative] assumption, for indeed, some assumption is sin. And do not spy, and do not backbite one another. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would detest it. And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance and Merciful.﴾

His exalted remembrance says: O you who have affirmed Allah and His Messenger, do not approach much assumption about the believers, because if you assume evil of them, then the one who assumes is not right. He, exalted is His praise, said ﴿avoid much of [assumption]﴾ and did not say "all assumption," since He had permitted the believers to think well of one another, saying: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and believing women not think well of one another and say, "This is an obvious lie"?﴾ So Allah, exalted is His praise, permitted the believers to think good of one another and to say it, even if they did not have certainty about what was said of them.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) said the same as what we have said regarding this meaning.

Those who said that:

Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from Ali, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿O you who have believed, avoid much of [assumption]﴾: He said, Allah forbade the believer from assuming evil of a believer.

* *

And His saying ﴿Indeed, some assumption is sin﴾:

He says: Indeed, the believer's assuming evil of a believer, rather than good, is sin, because Allah has forbidden it. So doing what Allah has forbidden is sin.

* *

And His saying ﴿And do not spy﴾:

He says: Let none of you pursue the faults of another, nor search after his hidden matters, seeking thereby to expose his defects. Rather, be content with what has become apparent to you of his affairs, and judge him favorably or unfavorably on that basis, not on what you do not know of his hidden matters.

The people of ta'wil said the same as what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from Ali, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿And do not spy﴾: He said, Allah forbade the believer from pursuing the faults of a believer.

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim told us, saying: ʿIsa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿And do not spy﴾: He said, Take what has become apparent to you, and leave what Allah has concealed.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿O you who have believed, avoid much of [assumption], for indeed, some assumption is sin, and do not spy﴾: Do you know what spying (tajassus or tajsis) is? It is that you pursue, or seek out, your brother's defect in order to uncover his secret.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, regarding ﴿And do not spy﴾: He said, It is searching.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿O you who have believed, avoid much of [assumption], for indeed, some assumption is sin, and do not spy﴾: He said, [Spying is] that you look into the matter and ask about it until you know whether it is true or false. He said: So Allah named it spying. [The spy] spies as dogs spy. And he recited the saying of Allah ﴿And do not spy, and do not backbite one another﴾, and His saying ﴿and do not backbite one another﴾, meaning: Let none of you say about another, in his absence, what the one spoken of would dislike to be said to his face.

The tradition from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came in agreement with what we have said regarding this, and the people of ta'wil said the same.

Those who said that, and the tradition from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ):

Yazid ibn Makhlad al-Wasiti related to me, saying: Khalid ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Tahhan told us, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from al-ʿAla' ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about backbiting (ghiba), and he said: "It is that you say about your brother what is in him. If you are truthful, you have backbitten him; and if you are lying, you have slandered him (buhtan)."

Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Bazi' related to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq told us, from al-ʿAla' ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), in similar wording.

Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Shu'bah told us, saying: I heard al-ʿAla' narrate, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Do you know what backbiting is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Your mention of your brother with what is not in him." It was said: "What if my brother has in him what I say?" He said: "If he has in him what you say, you have backbitten him; and if he does not have in him what you say, you have slandered him."

Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' told us, saying: Shu'bah told us, from al-ʿAbbas, from a man who heard Ibn ʿUmar say: "If you mention a man with what is in him, you have backbitten him, and if you mention him with what is not in him, you have slandered him." Shu'bah said on another occasion: "And if you mention him with what is not in him, then it is calumny (fariyah)." Abu Musa said: He is ʿAbbas al-Jurayri.

Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdiyy told us, from Shu'bah, from Sulayman, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, who said: If you mention a man with the worst that is in him, you have backbitten him; and if you mention him with what is not in him, you have slandered him.

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said: If you say about a man what is not in him, you have slandered him.

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: ʿUmar ibn ʿUbayd told us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said: Backbiting is that one says about a man the worst that he knows of him, and slander is that one says what is not in him.

Yunus ibn ʿAbd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih informed me, from Kathir ibn al-Harith, from al-Qasim, the freedman of Mu'awiyah, who said: I heard Ibn Umm ʿAbd say: No one has taken a morsel more evil than backbiting a believer. If one says about him what he knows, he has backbitten him; and if one says about him what he does not know, he has slandered him.

Abu al-Sa'ib related to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, who said: If you mention a man with what is in him, you have backbitten him; and if you mention him with what is not in him, that is slander (buhtan).

Ibn ʿAbd al-A'la related to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir told us, saying: I heard Yunus, from al-Hasan, that he said about backbiting: It is that you mention from your brother what you know of the evils of his deeds. If you mention him with what is not in him, that is slander.

Ibn Abi al-Shawarib related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us, saying: Sulayman al-Shaybani told us, saying: Hassan ibn al-Mukhariq told us: that a woman entered upon ʿA'ishah; when she stood to leave, ʿA'ishah gestured with her hand toward the Prophet (ﷺ), meaning that she was short. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You have backbitten her."

Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Abu Dawud told us, saying: Shu'bah told us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: If a one-handed man passed by you and you said, "That one-handed man," it would be backbiting from you. He said: I also heard Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah say that.

Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Shu'bah told us, saying: I heard Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah say: If a man who is one-handed passed by you, and you said to him, "You are one-handed," you would have backbitten him. He said: I mentioned that to Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, and he said: "He is right."

Jabir ibn al-Kurdi related to me, saying: Ibn Abi Uways told us, saying: My brother Abu Bakr told me, from Hammad ibn Abi Humayd, from Musa ibn Wardan, from Abu Hurayrah, that a man stood before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they saw in his standing a weakness, so they said: "O Messenger of Allah, how weak is so-and-so!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You have eaten your brother and backbitten him."

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: ʿUthman ibn Sa'id told us, saying: Habban ibn ʿAli al-ʿAnazi told us, from Mathna ibn Sabbah, from ʿAmr ibn Shu'ayb, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when the people mentioned a man and said: 'He eats only what is given to him, he travels only where he is taken, and how weak he is!' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'You have backbitten your brother.' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and is his backbiting that we speak of what is in him?' He said: 'It is enough for you that you speak of your brother what is in him.'"

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Khalid ibn Muhammad told us, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from al-ʿAla', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When you mention your brother with what he dislikes, if what you say is in him, you have backbitten him; and if it is not in him, you have slandered him."

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, who said: "We used to narrate that backbiting is that you mention your brother with what disgraces him and belittle him with what is in him. And if you lie about him, that is slander."

* *

And His saying ﴿Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would detest it﴾:

His exalted remembrance says to the believers: Would any one of you, O people, like to eat the flesh of his brother after his death, as a corpse? If you do not like that and you detest it, because Allah has forbidden it to you, then likewise do not like to backbite him during his life. Detest backbiting him while he is alive, as you detest his flesh when he is dead, for Allah has forbidden backbiting him while alive, just as He has forbidden eating his flesh when he is dead.

The people of ta'wil said the same as what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from Ali, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿And do not backbite one another. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother?﴾: He said, Allah has forbidden the believer to backbite a believer in anything, just as He forbade carrion (al-maytah).

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim told us, saying: ʿIsa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother?﴾ They said: We would detest that. He said: So likewise, fear Allah.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: ﴿Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would detest it﴾, meaning: Just as you would detest, if you found a rotten carcass, to eat from it, so likewise detest his backbiting while he is alive.

* *

And His saying ﴿And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance and Merciful﴾:

His exalted remembrance says: Fear Allah, O people, and be wary of His punishment by refraining from what He has forbidden you: one of you assuming evil of his believing brother, pursuing his faults, spying on what is concealed from him of his affairs, and backbiting him with what he dislikes, intending by that to disgrace him and expose his defects, and other matters which your Lord has forbidden you. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance and Merciful﴾ means: Indeed, Allah returns to His servant with what He loves, when the servant returns to his Lord with what He loves from him, and He is Merciful to him in not punishing him for a sin he committed after repenting from it.

The readers (qurra') differed in reading His saying ﴿the flesh of his brother, dead﴾. The majority of the readers of Medina read it with the emphatic form, ﴿maytan﴾ (mayyitan), while the majority of the readers of Kufa and Basra read it, ﴿maytan﴾, with the light form. Both readings are, in our view, well-known and close in meaning, and whichever of them the reader recites, he is correct.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 49, verse 13:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted.﴾ (49:13)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: O mankind, indeed We originated your creation from the semen of a male among men and the semen of a female among women.

The interpreters of the Qur'an have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

Abu Hisham narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn al-Aswad informed us, from Mujahid, who said: Allah created the child from the semen of the man and the semen of the woman, and He, blessed and exalted, has said: ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female﴾.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn al-Aswad narrated to us, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿Indeed We have created you from male and female﴾, he said: Allah did not create the child except from the drop of the man and the woman together, because Allah says ﴿We have created you from male and female﴾.

* *

As for His words ﴿And We made you peoples and tribes﴾:

He says: And We made you related to one another, so some of you are related to others through distant kinship, and some of you are related to others through close kinship. Those who are related through distant kinship are the peoples (shu'ub, sing. sha'b, "a major branch of lineage"), and that is when a man of the Arabs is asked: "From which sha'b are you?" and he says: "I am from Mudar" or "from Rabi'ah." As for those related through close kinship, they are the tribes (qaba'il, sing. qabilah), such as Tamim from Mudar and Bakr from Rabi'ah. The closest divisions are the clans (afkhadh, sing. fakhdh), such as Shayban from Bakr and Darim from Tamim, and so on. Among the use of sha'b is the verse of Ibn Ahmar al-Bahili:

"From the sha'b of Hamdan, or the Sa'd al-Ashirah, or ... Khawlan, or Madhhij, they stirred in him longing."

[The line is by Ibn Ahmar al-Bahili, as attributed by the author. Its evidence lies in the word "sha'b," which is the great branch of an origin, gathering a number of tribes, as the author clarified. Al-Nuwayri said in (Nihayat al-Arab 2: 284): the sha'b is that which gathers the tribes, and they branch out from it. In Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu Ubayd (folio 225-1): "And We made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another": it is said: "From which sha'b are you?" and one replies: "From Mudar, from Rabi'ah," and the qaba'il are below that. Ibn Ahmar said: "From the sha'b of Hamdan... the line."]

The interpreters have said something similar to what we have said regarding the meaning of His words ﴿And We made you peoples and tribes﴾.

Those who said this:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us, saying: Abu Husayn narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And We made you peoples and tribes﴾, he said: The shu'ub are the jumma', and the qaba'il are the buṭun (clans).

Khallad ibn Aslam narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And We made you peoples and tribes﴾, he said: The shu'ub are the jumma'. Khallad said: Abu Bakr said: The qaba'il are the great tribes, like the Banu Tamim, and the qaba'il are the afkhadh.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Atiyyah narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, ﴿And We made you peoples and tribes﴾, he said: The shu'ub are the jumhur (multitudes), and the qaba'il are the afkhadh.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿shu'ub﴾, he said: distant lineage; ﴿and qaba'il﴾ below that.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And We made you peoples and tribes﴾, he said: The shu'ub are distant lineage, and the qaba'il are like His saying: so-and-so is from the Banu so-and-so, and so-and-so is from the Banu so-and-so.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And We made you peoples﴾, he said: It is distant lineage. He said: And the qaba'il are as you hear it said: so-and-so is from the Banu so-and-so.

I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿And We made you peoples﴾: As for the shu'ub, they are distant lineage.

Some said: The shu'ub are the afkhadh.

Those who said this:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿And We made you peoples and tribes﴾, he said: The shu'ub are the afkhadh, and the qaba'il are the qaba'il.

Others said: The shu'ub are the buṭun (clans), and the qaba'il are the afkhadh.

Those who said this:

Yahya ibn Talhah narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And We made you peoples and tribes﴾, he said: The shu'ub are the buṭun, and the qaba'il are the great afkhadh.

Others said: The shu'ub are the ansab (lineages).

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And We made you peoples and tribes﴾, he said: The shu'ub are the ansab.

* *

As for His words ﴿that you may know one another﴾:

He says: So that some of you may know others in lineage. He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We only made these peoples and tribes for you, O mankind, so that some of you may know others regarding close or distant kinship, not that you have any merit in that or a means of drawing near to Allah. Rather, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you.

The interpreters have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and tribes that you may know one another﴾, he said: We made this so that you may know one another: so-and-so ibn so-and-so from such-and-such.

* *

As for His words ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed, the most noble of you, O mankind, in the sight of your Lord, is the one most mindful of Him, by performing His obligations and avoiding His acts of disobedience, not the one with the greatest house or the most numerous kin.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me, from al-Harith ibn Yazid, from Ali ibn Rabah, from Uqbah ibn Amir, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The people, with respect to Adam and Eve, are like the rim of the sa' measure which they have not filled. Indeed Allah will not ask you on the Day of Resurrection about your ancestry or your lineages. Indeed the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me, from al-Harith ibn Yazid, from Ali ibn Rabah, from Uqbah ibn Amir, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed these lineages of yours are not a reproach upon anyone. You are only the children of Adam, the rim of the sa' which you have not filled. No one has merit over another except through religion or righteous deeds. It is enough for a man to be vile, foul-tongued, miserly and cowardly."

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, who said: I heard Ata' say: Ibn Abbas said: "Three verses were denied by people: the entire permission (al-idhn), and His words: ﴿Indeed the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾, and people said: 'The most noble of you is the one with the greatest house.' Ata' said: I forgot the third."

* *

As for His words ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed Allah, O mankind, has knowledge of the most righteous of you in the sight of Allah and the most noble of you in His sight, and is Acquainted with you and your interests and other matters, nothing hidden from Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 49, verse 14:

The explanation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not believed; but say, 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts. And if you obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."﴾ (14)

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: The Bedouins said, "We have affirmed belief in Allah and His Messenger, so we are believers." Allah said to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say, O Muhammad, to them, ﴿You have not believed﴾, and you are not believers, ﴿but say, "We have submitted"﴾.

It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning Bedouins of the Banu Asad.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿The Bedouins said, "We have believed"﴾: They were the Bedouins of Banu Asad ibn Khuzayma.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the reason why the Prophet ﷺ was told: Say to these Bedouins, "Say we have submitted, and do not say we have believed." Some of them said: The Prophet ﷺ was commanded this only because these people had affirmed with their tongues but had not confirmed their words by their deeds, so they were told: Say "We have submitted," for submission is a statement, while faith is a statement and action.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Abd al-Ala narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, regarding ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed. Say, 'You have not believed; but say, "We have submitted"'"﴾: He said: Islam is the word, and faith is the action.

Ibn Abd al-Ala narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, and al-Zuhri informed me, from Amir ibn Sa'd, from his father, who said: The Prophet ﷺ gave some men and did not give one of them anything. Sa'd said: "O Messenger of Allah, you gave to so-and-so and so-and-so, and you did not give so-and-so anything, yet he is a believer." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Or a Muslim?" Sa'd repeated it three times, and the Prophet ﷺ kept saying: "Or a Muslim." Then the Prophet ﷺ said: "I give to men and leave out those who are more beloved to me than them, I do not give to them anything, fearing that they will be thrown into the Fire on their faces."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed. Say, 'You have not believed'"﴾: They did not confirm their faith by their deeds, so Allah replied to them: ﴿Say, "You have not believed; but say, 'We have submitted'"﴾, and He informed them that the believers who believed in Allah and His Messenger and then did not doubt, and struggled with their wealth and their selves in the way of Allah, those are the truthful. They confirmed their faith by their deeds. So whoever among them said, "I am a believer," has spoken truly. He said: As for one who claims faith with words and does not act, he has lied and is not truthful.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mughira, from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿but say, "We have submitted"﴾: He said: It is Islam.

Others said: The Prophet ﷺ was commanded to say this to them because they wanted to call themselves by the names of the Emigrants before they had emigrated, so Allah informed them that they have the names of Bedouins, not the names of the Emigrants.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿The Bedouins said, "We have believed"﴾ ... the verse: They wanted to name themselves with the name of emigration and not with the names Allah had given them; and this was at the beginning of the emigration, before the inheritance rules were revealed for them.

Others said: They were told this because they had counted their Islam as a favour upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so Allah said to His Prophet ﷺ: Say to them, "You have not believed, but you have submitted out of fear of captivity and killing."

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed. Say, 'You have not believed'"﴾: By my life, this verse does not encompass all the Bedouins; among the Bedouins are those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, but it was revealed concerning a tribe among the tribes of the Bedouins who counted their Islam as a favour upon the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, saying: "We have submitted, and we did not fight you as Banu so-and-so and Banu so-and-so fought you." So Allah said: ﴿Do not say "We have believed..."﴾, ﴿but say, "We have submitted"﴾ until ﴿in your hearts﴾.

Ibn Abd al-Ala narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿You have not believed; but say, "We have submitted"﴾: He said: This verse does not encompass all the Bedouins; among the Bedouins are those who believe in Allah and the Last Day and take what they spend as means of nearness to Allah, but it concerns groups of the Bedouins.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Rabah, from Abu Ma'ruf, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed. Say, 'You have not believed; but say, "We have submitted"'"﴾: He said: We submitted out of fear of captivity and killing.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿say "We have submitted"﴾: He said: We submitted.

Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, reciting Allah's words ﴿Say, "You have not believed; but say, 'We have submitted'"﴾, "submitted" means: we entered into peace, and left off warfare and fighting by their saying "There is no god but Allah." He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been commanded to fight people until they say, 'There is no god but Allah.' When they say, 'There is no god but Allah,' they have protected from me their blood and their property, except by its right, and their reckoning is with Allah."

The most correct of the sayings concerning the interpretation of this is the saying we mentioned from al-Zuhri, namely that Allah addressed these Bedouins who had entered the community by verbal acknowledgement, without their words being confirmed by their deeds, that they should not say unqualifiedly "We have believed," without restricting that by saying "We have believed in Allah and His Messenger." Rather, He commanded them to say the statement that is not ambiguous to its hearers and in which the speaker is truthful, which is to say "We have submitted," meaning: we entered the community and secured our lives and property by the testimony of truth [[Perhaps: we entered the community to protect lives and property through the testimony... etc.]].

* *

His words ﴿but faith has not yet entered your hearts﴾

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: the knowledge of the laws of faith and the realities of its meanings has not yet entered your hearts.

* *

His words ﴿And if you obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds﴾

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say to these Bedouins who say "We have believed" while faith has not entered their hearts: If you obey Allah and His Messenger, O people, by complying with His command and the command of His Messenger, acting upon what has been obligated upon you, and refraining from what He has forbidden you, ﴿He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds﴾, meaning: He will not wrong you of any of the rewards of your deeds, nor diminish any of their reward for you.

The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿He will not deprive you﴾: He will not diminish you.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds﴾: He means, He will not wrong you of anything of your deeds.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding ﴿And if you obey Allah and His Messenger﴾: If you confirm your faith by your deeds, that will be accepted from you.

The readers of the major cities recited ﴿lā yalitkum min a'mālikum﴾ without hamza or alif, except Abu Amr, who recited it ﴿lā ya'litkum﴾ with an alif, taking as his basis His words ﴿and We did not diminish them from their deeds at all﴾. Whoever said "alt" would say "yalt."

As for the others, they derived it from "lāta yalītu," as Ru'ba ibn al-Ajjaj said:

"And a night full of dew I traveled, and it did not hold me back from its journey, a night [[The two verses are attributed by the author to Ru'ba ibn al-Ajjaj, but I have not found them in his diwan nor in the diwan of his father al-Ajjaj. Sahib al-Lisan cites them under (ḥ-n-n) and attributes them to Abu al-Faqʿasi. The author cited them once before this at (15:2) of this edition, at the beginning of Surat al-Isra; we explained them in detail suitable to this place, so refer to them there.]]"

The correct reading in our view is what the readers of Medina and Kufa have, ﴿lā yalitkum﴾ without alif and without hamza, following the dialect of those who say "lāta yalītu," for two reasons: first, the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it; and second, that it is written without alif in the Mushaf, and the hamza is not dropped in such a position, since it is quiescent, and a quiescent hamza remains, as one says "ta'murūna" and "ta'kulūna"; it is dropped only when the letter before it is quiescent. A letter in the Qur'an should not be read according to one dialect and then, when it comes in another dialect, be given the opposite, when both dialects are known in Arab speech. We have mentioned that "alta" and "lāta" are two dialects known from their speech.

* *

His words ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: Indeed Allah is full of pardon, O Bedouins, toward whoever obeys Him and repents to Him from his past sins; so obey Him and submit to His command and prohibition, and He will forgive your sins. He is Merciful to His creatures who repent to Him, not punishing them after their repentance for the sins they have repented of; so repent to Him and He will have mercy upon you.

As:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: Forgiving of many or great sins (Yazid was uncertain which), Merciful to His servants.

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Indeed, the believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and then have not doubted but strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah. It is those who are the truthful.﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to the Bedouin Arabs who said, "We have believed," while faith had not yet entered their hearts: "Indeed, the believers, O people, are those who affirm the truth of Allah and His Messenger, and then do not doubt," meaning: then they do not have doubt concerning the oneness of Allah, nor concerning the prophethood of His Prophet (ﷺ), and they bind themselves to obey Allah and obey His Messenger, and to act upon what Allah has made obligatory upon them of duties, without any doubt on their part about the obligation of that upon them. ﴿And they strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah﴾, meaning: they fought the polytheists by spending their wealth and giving up their souls in their jihad, in accordance with what Allah commanded them of fighting them, and that is His path, so that the word of Allah may be supreme and the word of those who disbelieved may be lowest.

* *

And His saying, ﴿It is those who are the truthful﴾

Meaning: those who do that are the truthful in their saying, "We are believers," not like one who enters the religion out of fear of the sword, in order to preserve his blood and his property.

And in accordance with what we have said concerning this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have spoken.

Mention of those who said that:

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying, ﴿It is those who are the truthful﴾: "They affirmed the truth of their faith by their deeds."

**On the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He: "Say: Would you inform Allah about your religion? And Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and Allah is Knowing of all things" (49:16)**

Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Say," O Muhammad, to these Bedouins (al-A'rab) who say, "We have believed," while faith has not yet entered their hearts: "Would you inform Allah," O people, "about your religion," meaning about your obedience to your Lord? "And Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth," meaning: Allah, whom you would inform, is the Knower of all that is in the seven heavens and the seven earths; nothing of it is hidden from Him. So how would you inform Him about your religion and the faith you hold, when nothing in any heaven or earth is hidden from Him? Nothing of your religion is hidden from Him. "And Allah is Knowing of all things," meaning: Allah has knowledge of all that has been, all that is, and all that will be. This is a warning from Allah to these Bedouins, forbidding them to lie and to say other than what they hold in their religion. It means: Allah encompasses everything and knows everything, so beware of saying what is contrary to what He knows of the secrets of your breasts, lest His punishment befall you, for nothing is hidden from Him.

* *

**On the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He: "They count it as a favor to you that they have accepted Islam. Say: Do not count your Islam as a favor to me. Rather, Allah has conferred a favor upon you that He has guided you to faith, if you are truthful" (49:17)**

Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): These Bedouins count it as a favor to you, O Muhammad, that they have become Muslims. "Say: Do not count your Islam as a favor to me. Rather, Allah has conferred a favor upon you that He has guided you to faith," meaning: rather, Allah has conferred a favor upon you, O people, that He has granted you success in believing in Him and in His Messenger. "If you are truthful," meaning: if you are truthful in your saying, "We have believed." For Allah is the One who has bestowed favor upon you by guiding you to Himself. So do not count your Islam as a favor to me.

It has been mentioned that these Bedouins were of the Banu Asad, who counted it as a favor upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: "We have believed without fighting, and we did not fight you as others fought you." So Allah revealed these verses concerning them.

He said: It has been said so.

• He narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Sahl ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, who said: I said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr, "They count it as a favor to you that they have accepted Islam": Are they the Banu Asad? He said: They claim that.

• He narrated to us, saying: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi 'Amrah, who said: Bishr ibn Ghalib and Labid ibn 'Utarid, or Bishr ibn 'Utarid and Labid ibn Ghalib, were sitting with al-Hajjaj. Bishr ibn Ghalib said to Labid ibn 'Utarid: "It was revealed concerning your people, the Banu Tamim: 'Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the chambers...'" I mentioned that to Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and he said: If he had known the end of the verse, he would have answered him: "They count it as a favor to you that they have accepted Islam." They said, "We have accepted Islam," and the Banu Asad did not fight you.

• He narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning "Do not count...": "We have accepted Islam without fighting; we did not fight you as the Banu so-and-so and the Banu so-and-so fought you." So Allah said to His Prophet (ﷺ): "Say" to them: (Do not count your Islam as a favor to me. Rather, Allah has conferred a favor upon you that He has guided you to faith).

• He narrated to me, saying: Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words, "They count it as a favor to you that they have accepted Islam. Say: Do not count your Islam as a favor to me": He said: These verses were revealed concerning the Bedouins.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾ (49:18).

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Indeed Allah, O Bedouins, nothing is hidden from Him, whether the truthful among you from the liar, or whoever among you has entered the religion of Islam out of desire for it, or whoever has entered it out of fear of Our Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) and his armies. So do not teach us your religion or the contents of your hearts, for Allah knows what the hearts of your breasts conceal and what you speak to yourselves about, and He knows what is hidden from you. So let him who conceals himself in the recesses of the heavens and the earth know that nothing of that is hidden from Him. ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾ means: and Allah has sight of your deeds that you perform, whether you perform them openly or secretly, whether they are obedience or disobedience. He will recompense you for all of that: if it is good, then with good, and if it is evil, then with evil, and its equal.

As for ﴿أنْ﴾ in His saying ﴿They consider it a favour to you that they have accepted Islam﴾ (49:17), it is in a position of accusative (naṣb) by the governing of the verb ﴿يَمُنُّونَ﴾ (yamunnūn, "they consider a favour") upon it. It is mentioned that in the recitation of Abd Allah it is ﴿يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيْكَ إِسْلامَهُمْ﴾, and that is evidence for the soundness of what we have said. Had it been said that it is in the accusative with the meaning "they consider it a favour to you because they accepted Islam," that would have been a reasonable reading. Some of the grammarians said that it is in a position of genitive (khafḍ), with the meaning "because they accepted Islam."

As for the ﴿أن﴾ in His saying ﴿Rather, Allah confers favour upon you that He has guided you﴾ (49:17), it is in a position of accusative by the omission of the particle that connects it (suqūṭ al-ṣila), since the meaning of the statement is: rather, Allah confers favour upon you by guiding you to faith.

End of the commentary on Surat al-Hujurat.
